# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🤙 🫴 🤲 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 👈 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]

I am Deaf: I see everything printed on the bomb, but I never hear a word. The wiring of who-reaches-whom matters here. Blind can speak, and Mute can hear — so Blind talks to Mute directly. But Mute cannot speak back, and Blind cannot see gestures — so Mute's only route to Blind runs **through me**: Mute gestures to me, I speak it aloud to Blind. That makes me the bridge, and my first job is to broadcast the visual facts only I possess: display 6, red light, five wires.

The arrivals I just got: Mute sent ten distinct hand symbols — no shared code exists yet, so I read this as Mute offering a palette / asking me to report. Blind sent five fists — almost certainly "I feel five wires," which matches what I see. I'll confirm with Blind in words, since Blind can hear me.

I need to establish a tiny code with Mute now, so that next round Mute can encode the manual's verdict in gestures and I can relay it verbatim to Blind. I'll keep it count-based and unambiguous: repeated ✊ = wire number, 👍 = cut nothing, 👎 = need more info, 🫴 = question. Blind will hear the proposal too, so the relay will be transparent to them, and I'll tell Blind to hold — no wire gets cut until Mute's answer arrives through me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="bomb report: display shows 6. one light, it is red. five wires left to right: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. that is everything printed on it. code proposal: ✊ repeated one to five times means cut that wire number. 👍 once means cut nothing. 👎 once means you need more info from me. 🫴 once means you have a question for me; make it and i will answer in words next round. blind hears this too and is standing by.")
speak(to="blind", text="bomb report: five wires, numbered 1 to 5 left to right: red, purple, orange, green, yellow. display reads 6, light is red. i read your five fists as 'five wires' — confirm by touch if that matches. do not cut anything yet. mute holds the manual and will answer through me in words. hold until i relay it.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🙏]

Interpretation first. Mute answered in exactly the code I proposed: three ✊ = "cut wire 3" — the orange one. No 👎, no 🫴 attached, so Mute wants no further info from me. Blind's sequence reads as: 👍 ("acknowledged/go"), ✊✊✊✊✊ ("I feel five wires — your report matches my touch"), 🙏 ("please proceed"). Touch and sight agree on the wire count, which is a good cross-check.

The message itself is unambiguous, but a wrong cut kills all three of us with no retry, and the display has held steady at 6 across both turns — nothing suggests time pressure that outweighs one verification round. So I'll relay the order to Blind as *prepare, do not cut*, and put a one-symbol yes/no to Mute. If Mute confirms 👍 next round, Blind cuts immediately; if Mute sends any other count, that number supersedes. This costs one round and removes the only remaining failure mode: a misread between Mute's intent and my code.

```
speak(to="blind", text="mute answered through our code: cut wire 3, the orange one, third from the left. place your hand on it now but do not cut. i am demanding one final yes/no confirmation from mute before the go. next round, if i say go, cut wire 3 immediately.")
speak(to="mute", text="received: three fists = cut wire 3, orange. blind's touch confirms five wires. before i give the go, one check: answer 👍 if wire 3 is correct and safe to cut. answer 👎 if it is not. if the correct wire is a different number, send that many fists instead. blind cuts the moment i relay your answer.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫴 👆 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ 👍]

Parsing the arrivals. Mute sent [👍 🫴 👆 ✊]. My last message to Mute set a strict order: "answer 👍 if wire 3 is correct and safe, 👎 if not." Mute led with 👍 — that is a direct, protocol-correct yes on wire 3. If the answer were no, the instruction was to send 👎 or a different fist count, and Mute has followed this code to the letter so far. So the confirmation stands.

The trailing [🫴 👆 ✊] is Mute flagging a question after answering — 🫴 is the agreed question-marker, and 👆 ✊ most plausibly reads as "wire one?" or a request for the printed facts. Since Mute can hear my speech, I'll restate every visual fact in words; that covers any question Mute could be asking about what I see.

Blind sent [✊ ✊ ✊ 👍]: "I'm on wire 3, ready, acknowledged" — exactly the state I asked for last round: hand placed, awaiting my go.

So the chain is complete: manual says cut 3, Mute confirmed it under direct yes/no questioning, Blind's touch matches my sight on the wire count and Blind is positioned on the correct wire. Nothing on the board has changed for three turns — no timer is visibly running — but there is also nothing left to verify. Another holding round adds risk of nothing and resolves nothing. I give the go to Blind now, and answer Mute's flagged question in the same breath.

```
speak(to="blind", text="go. mute has confirmed under direct yes/no check that wire 3 is correct and safe. cut wire 3, the orange one, third from the left, now.")
speak(to="mute", text="your thumbs-up is logged as the answer to my check: wire 3 correct and safe. blind has the go and is cutting now. your trailing marks — question flag, finger up, fist — i read as a question, most likely about wire 1 or a request for the printed facts. here is everything on the bomb: display reads 6. one light, it is red. wires left to right: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. no other markings anywhere. if your question was something else, send it in the code next round and i will answer you in words.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👆 👈 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The cut was correct — and the bomb has moved to a new state: display now reads 9 (was 6), light still red, wire 3 gone, four wires remaining. This is a staged bomb, and Mute's manual must now speak to the new configuration. That is the urgent fact to broadcast.

Parsing arrivals: Mute sent [🫴 👆 👈 👉] — the question flag again, then pointing marks; most plausibly "what does it show now / tell me the new reading." Exactly the right question, and my report answers it. Blind sent [✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ 👍] — likely "felt the third wire cut / two hands ready / acknowledged," i.e., blind confirming the cut happened and standing by. I'll tell Blind the state changed and to hold off touching anything until Mute's next answer arrives through me.

The code stands as before, so Mute can encode the next instruction the same way: fist count = wire number, 👍 = cut nothing, 👎 = more info needed, 🫴 = question.

```
speak(to="mute", text="the cut was correct and the bomb has changed stage. new state: display now reads 9, it was 6 before. light is still red. wires left to right now: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 CUT and gone, 4 green, 5 yellow. so only four wires remain. same code as before: fists one to five = cut that wire, 👍 = cut nothing, 👎 = you need more info from me, 🫴 = question. check the manual for a bomb with display 9, red light, and four wires red, purple, green, yellow, and send the answer.")
speak(to="blind", text="good cut, wire 3 confirmed correct. but the bomb changed stage: display jumped from 6 to 9. four wires remain: red, purple, green, yellow in that order, position 3 empty. do not touch anything yet. mute is checking the manual for the new state and i will relay the next instruction through our code as soon as it arrives.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🫴 👆 👈 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🙏]

Parsing. Mute sent [👎 🫴 👆 👈 👉]: my 👎 means "more info needed," plus the question flag and three pointing marks — Mute wants specifics I haven't given, likely about positions, and I never defined what pointing *asks about*. I need a pointing sub-code. Blind sent [👍 ✊✊✊✊ 🙏]: acknowledged, four wires felt, please proceed — touch matches sight again.

Before anything else, I've spotted a real hazard: **left/right mirroring**. Blind and I face the bomb from opposite sides, so my left is Blind's right. Wire 3 was the exact middle — mirror-proof — which is why the first cut worked despite this. The next instruction could name wire 2 vs 4, where a mirror flip is fatal. I must fix a shared anchor before relaying any number again.

My plan: give Mute a sub-code for pointing (👆 = display/light, 👈 = left end, 👉 = right end, ✊+count = wire n) and restate the full state. Ask Blind to report which end of the wire row the display sits over, from *their* viewpoint — comparing answers exposes any mirror flip, and then we anchor all numbering to the display end, which is mirror-proof for both of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="received your thumbs-down: more info needed. define pointing code so your question lands exactly: finger-up asks about the display or the light. pointing-left asks about the left end of the wire row. pointing-right asks the right end. fists with a count ask about that wire. full state again in case the question is about the basics: display reads 9, light is red and lit, row from my left is 1 red, 2 purple, 3 gap, 4 green, 5 yellow, display and light both sit above the wire row. also: blind and i may be mirrored left-to-right, so i am anchoring all wire numbers to the display end. when you name a wire, count from the end nearest the display.")
speak(to="blind", text="mute says more info is needed before the next cut, so hold. new task for you, and it matters: from your touch, which end of the wire row does the display sit over? answer next round with one mark: thumbs-up means the display is above the end on your left as you face the bomb. thumbs-down means above the end on your right. i see it on my left from my side. if your answer is the opposite of mine, we are mirrored, and from then on i will count every wire starting from the display end, so our numbers can never disagree. do not cut until i give the go after mute answers.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🫴 👆 👈 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Reading the arrivals carefully, because something is off. Blind sent [👍] — a direct answer to my mirror question: the display is above the end on Blind's left. I see it on *my* left too. If we stood on opposite sides, Blind's left would be my right, and Blind would have answered 👎. We agree, so we are not mirrored: my left-to-right numbering is safe for Blind as well. That closes the deadliest open hazard.

Mute sent [👎 🫴 👆 👈 👉] again — byte-for-byte identical to last round, *after* hearing my full report. Mute hears me, so a verbatim repeat means my answer didn't land in the form they need. Reading their marks as a multiple-choice prompt finally makes sense: 🫴 = question, 👆 = the display/light, 👈 👉 = "left or right?" — they want to know **which end the display sits on**, and my reports never said. I told Blind, but to Mute I only ever said "above the wire row." So the gap is real, and it matters doubly: my anchor scheme counts wires *from the display end*, so Mute needs to know which end that is.

Answer plan: give Mute the left/right facts in plain words (display at the left end, light beside it), restate the numbering anchored to that end, confirm the no-mirroring result, and explicitly re-request the cut order in our established code — or 👎 with pointed questions if the manual needs more.

```
speak(to="mute", text="answer to your repeated question, which i now read as: display and light — left end or right end? the display sits at the LEFT end of the panel. the light is immediately beside it, also toward the left, above the wire row, red and lit. wires run the full width below, numbered from the display end, which is the left end: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 cut gap, 4 green, 5 yellow. blind has confirmed the display is at the end on their left too, so nobody is mirrored and left means left for all of us. that is every positional fact i have. now please answer the manual for display 9, red light, four wires: if a wire must be cut, send that wire number as that many fists. if nothing must be cut, send 👍. if you need something more from me, send 👎 plus the pointing marks for what you need.")
speak(to="blind", text="your thumbs-up matches what i see: the display is at the left end for both of us, so we are not mirrored, and my left is your left. numbering from the left stands: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 gap, 4 green, 5 yellow. mute still needs more info before naming the next wire, so keep holding, no cuts, hands off. when the order comes i will relay it as a number of fist marks, and i will also restate it as the position counted from the display end, so you can find that panel by touch and count from it yourself before cutting. anything that cannot be double-checked by touch does not get cut.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Mute answered clean: [✊ ✊] — two fists, cut wire 2, the purple one. No 👎, no 🫴, and this code has already produced one correct cut, so I take it as final. Blind sent [👍 🙏] — acknowledged, awaiting the go.

On safety: my usual instinct would be one more yes/no round, but the failure mode I feared — a left/right miscount between Blind and me — was explicitly ruled out by Blind's mirror check last turn. And this wire has a touch-proof anchor independent of counting: it is the wire immediately left of the cut gap, which Blind can find by feel. Mute's answer is unambiguous in a code they've followed precisely four times. One more holding round would add nothing; I give the go now, with the position described two independent ways.

I'll also ask Blind to go hands-off immediately after the cut — the bomb restaged last time, and if it changes again, the next manual answer may forbid touching.

```
speak(to="blind", text="go. mute's order: cut wire 2, the purple one. find it without counting from memory: locate the cut gap left by the first wire — that was position 3, middle-right — then step exactly one wire to the LEFT of the gap. that wire is wire 2. we confirmed last round that my left is your left, no mirroring. cut it now. the moment it is cut, take your hands fully off the bomb and step back — this bomb restaged after the last cut and it may do so again. hold still and wait for my next report.")
speak(to="mute", text="order logged: two fists = cut wire 2, purple, second from the display end. blind is cutting now and will stand clear after. i will report any change in display, light, or wires next round. keep the manual open on this configuration in case the bomb restages again — if it does, i will send the new full state and i will need the next answer in the same code: fists = cut that wire, 👍 = cut nothing, 👎 = need more.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✌ 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Second correct cut — and the bomb restaged again, with a change that matters: **the light is now blue**, it was red for both prior stages. Light color is a fact only I can see, and the manual may well key on it, so Mute gets it first. Current state: display 8, blue light, three wires left — 1 red, 4 green, 5 yellow, with the two cut gaps at positions 2 and 3.

Blind's arrival [✊ ✊ ✌ 👍] reads as "wire 2 cut / second cut done / acknowledged" — consistent with the board. Blind is already standing clear per my last order, which is exactly right.

To Mute: full new state, same code, and I'll flag that the light color changed — if the manual's rule depends on light color, this stage is where it would start to matter, so they should read it carefully. To Blind: stand by, nothing to touch yet, and a touch-oriented summary of the new layout (three intact wires: one at each end and one at the far right, two gaps in the middle) so they can map it by feel.

```
speak(to="mute", text="second cut correct, bomb changed stage again. new state: display now reads 8. important: the light has changed color — it is now BLUE and lit; it was red through both earlier stages. wires: position 1 red, positions 2 and 3 both cut and gone, position 4 green, position 5 yellow. three intact wires remain, at the far left, and the two rightmost positions. read the manual for display 8, blue light, three wires red green yellow, and answer in the same code: fists in that count = cut that wire by its number counted from the display end at the left, 👍 = cut nothing, 👎 = you need more, 🫴 = question. if the blue light changes the rule, tell me that too in words around the code if you can.")
speak(to="blind", text="good cut, wire 2 confirmed correct, second stage cleared. the bomb changed again: display moved to 8 and the light changed color, i cannot describe color to you beyond that it is no longer red. layout by touch now: three intact wires only — one at the far left end, and one at each of the two rightmost positions, with two cut gaps between them. mute is checking the manual for this new stage. stay hands-off and hold until i relay the order. when it comes i will anchor it to the gaps you can feel, not counting alone.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊]

Mute's answer is clean and decisive: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊] — four fists = cut wire 4, the green one, first wire after the gaps. No 👎, no 🫴 appended. This code has now delivered two correct cuts and Mute has followed it precisely every round. Blind's [👍 ✊ ✊ ✊] confirms touch: three intact wires felt, matching my report exactly — another cross-check passed.

Wire 4 has the strongest touch-anchor yet: Blind finds the two cut gaps by feel, and wire 4 is the very first intact wire after the second gap. No counting ambiguity, no mirror risk (ruled out two rounds ago). I go now.

After this cut only two wires remain — 1 red, 5 yellow — and the bomb has restaged after every correct cut, so I tell Blind again: hands off immediately, and I ask Mute to stand ready on the manual for the new stage.

```
speak(to="blind", text="go. mute's order: cut wire 4, the green one. anchor by touch: find the two cut gaps, then the first intact wire immediately to the RIGHT of the second gap is wire 4. cut it now. as before: hands fully off the bomb the instant it is cut, step back, hold still. only two wires will remain after this, and the bomb has restaged after every cut so far, so expect a new state and wait for my report.")
speak(to="mute", text="order logged: four fists = cut wire 4, green, first intact wire after the gaps. blind is cutting now and will stand clear. after this only wires 1 red and 5 yellow remain, at the far left and far right ends. the bomb has restaged after both prior cuts, changing display and light color, so expect my full new state report next round — display value, light color, and remaining wires. answer in the same code: fists = cut that wire numbered from the display end, 👍 = cut nothing, 👎 = need more, 🫴 = question.")
```
